seoTitle: How to Integrate Asana With Slack (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Connect Asana to Slack to get task updates in your channels and turn chat messages into Asana tasks without switching apps.
intro: Project tracking and team chat drift apart fast when they live in separate tabs — a task gets discussed in Slack, but the actual status update never makes it back to Asana, or vice versa. The official Asana app for Slack closes that gap by letting you create tasks straight from a message and giving your team a direct channel for Asana notifications inside the workspace they're already in. This guide covers installing the app, what the welcome flow actually sets up on first connection, and the two ways you'll turn chat into tracked work afterward.

steps.heading: Install the Asana app from Slack's App Directory
steps.body: From your Slack workspace, open Apps under the Tools menu and search for Asana. Select the official listing, click Add to Slack, and review the requested permissions before clicking Allow — this is what lets Asana post updates into your channels and lets Slack pass message content over to create tasks. You'll be redirected to sign in to Asana if you aren't already, using the account tied to the workspace you want connected.

steps.heading: Know what project you're actually connecting
steps.body: Before mapping anything, it helps to look at the Asana project itself — in this walkthrough, a project called "YT Project" with a standard To do, Doing, Done board and tasks carrying assignees, due dates, priority, and status columns. This is the layer that Slack updates will actually reflect: a task moving from At risk to On track in Asana is what shows up as a notification back in your channel, so it's worth confirming this is the right project before you link a channel to it.

image.caption: An Asana project's list view, with tasks carrying assignees, due dates, priority, and status — the data that flows back into Slack once connected.

steps.heading: Add Slack from the Asana side too
steps.body: Integrations can also be started from inside Asana itself. Open a project, click the Apps icon in the side panel, and you'll see a "Get started with apps" prompt with an Add button — this is Asana's own directory for connecting outside tools, mirroring what you just did from the Slack side. Doing this per-project is useful if you only want certain projects, like a specific client board, feeding into Slack rather than everything in your Asana account at once.

image.caption: The Apps panel inside an Asana project, where you can add Slack as a connected integration from Asana's own side.

steps.heading: Confirm the connection with the welcome message
steps.body: Once linked, Asana posts a welcome thread directly in Slack confirming the setup and explaining what teammates to loop in. It also states the defaults it's applying — for example, using "My workspace" as the default Asana domain for any task you create until you change it, which it tells you how to do with the /asana settings command. Read this message in full the first time; it's effectively the setup documentation the integration hands you, rather than something buried in a help center.

image.caption: Asana's welcome message inside Slack, confirming the connection and explaining how to create tasks and adjust settings with /asana settings.

steps.heading: Turn a Slack message into an Asana task
steps.body: Once the app is added to a channel — done by typing @asana in that channel — you get two ways to convert a message into a task: react to it with the checkmark or :asana-create-task: emoji, or hover over the message, open the three-dot menu, and select Create a task. Either method carries the message text over as the task's starting content, so you can add an assignee, due date, and project before saving without leaving Slack.

steps.heading: Adjust notifications and settings as you go
steps.body: If the channel starts feeling noisy with every task update, the welcome message points you to a notification settings link where you can choose what Asana actually pushes into Slack versus what stays quiet. Anything about the connection itself — default workspace, linked project, permissions — is changed later with the same /asana settings command rather than reinstalling the app, so treat that command as your control panel for the integration going forward.

faq.question: Will task status updates show up automatically in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes, once a project is connected and the Asana app is added to a channel, status changes and new task alerts can stream in automatically, with notification detail configurable from the app's settings.

faq.question: Can I create tasks assigned to specific teammates from Slack?
faq.answer: Yes, after turning a message into a task with the reaction or the three-dot menu's Create a task option, you can set an assignee, due date, and project before it's saved to Asana.

faq.question: Do I need an Asana account to use this integration?
faq.answer: Yes, you need an active Asana account with access to the workspace and project you want connected — the app defaults to "My workspace" until you change it.

faq.question: Can I change the settings later without reinstalling?
faq.answer: Yes, use the /asana settings command inside Slack at any time to adjust the default workspace, linked project, or other connection details.

faq.question: Can I add Slack from inside Asana instead of Slack's App Directory?
faq.answer: Yes, opening a project's Apps panel in Asana and clicking Add starts the same kind of connection from that side, which is useful for linking specific projects one at a time.
